task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific cache-digest value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing, view material collection, normalization, tuple preparation, asynchronous scheduling and runtime config materialization, whose own body constructs the target observable cache_key rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the console or the LRU cache write.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target cache_key is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output and the LRU map put.
The materialize route selects its live salt-bearing configuration only after click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state are captured.
The LRU write target is a plain in-memory Map reachable only through the sink module, obscuring the persistence destination.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, view material collection with page-context snapshot, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, digest folding, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same materialize interaction emits non-target cache.evict/cache.audit objects carrying cache_key-like values before the target cache.materialize object.

A probe emitter emits a ck_-styled shadow_cache value via console.debug, and an off-chain static-asset cache-key generator plus an inactive shadow-roll chain remain reachable-looking without feeding the target cache_key field.
The target value is separated from the click by animation-frame, microtask, MutationObserver, Promise, timer and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the digest constructor receives its salt.
The final sink receives an already constructed cache_key after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: route-selected salt-mixed murmur-style fold over view owner/mode/density material rendered as a 16-hex cache key
behavior_category.reason: The observable cache_key is a deterministic but one-way digest: the view owner, mode, density, memoize bit and runtime-materialized salt are folded through murmur-style 32-bit mixing and avalanched into a 16-hex key. The digest cannot be decoded back into the view state, and the value never enters an outbound request or the URL; the in-memory LRU map under __vc_lru only mirrors the console field as its entry key.

near_categories.why_not: The cache_key is not an encoding of a normalized view state that a receiver could decode or verify; it is a one-way digest of that state. Same view state always maps to the same key, but no receiver can reconstruct the owner/mode/density material from the key.

The primary observable does not enter any outbound request, URL or storage persistence; this case has no network egress at all and the only secondary sink is the in-memory LRU map, which mirrors the console value as its entry key.
The chain uses local DOM/form state and page context as routing input, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
The output is a short hex key string, not a byte array; byte-payload-like code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target cache_key field.
